title: A closed immersion induces an isomorphism on residue fields
statement: Let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion], let $z\in Z$, and put $x=i(z)$. The homomorphism of residue fields $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(z)$ induced by $i$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Schemes, Tag 01HJ-area (stalk maps and residue fields for morphisms of locally ringed spaces), together with Morphisms, Lemma Tag 01QO (closed-immersion affine quotient criterion)

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $B=\mathcal O_{Z,z}$. The closed immersion gives a surjective sheaf map $i^\sharp:\mathcal O_X\twoheadrightarrow i_*\mathcal O_Z$ by the definition of a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] (Stacks Morphisms 01QO). By [lem-weil-pbc-locally-surjective-iff-stalks], its stalk map at $x$, $A\to(i_*\mathcal O_Z)_x$, is surjective. The stalk-bijection [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks](2) gives a bijection $c_z:(i_*\mathcal O_Z)_x\xrightarrow{\sim}B$. Under this bijection, the composite $A\to(i_*\mathcal O_Z)_x\xrightarrow{c_z}B$ is the stalk map $i^\sharp_z$ (the germ formula for $i^\sharp$); it is a local homomorphism because $i$ is a morphism of locally ringed spaces [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. Hence $i^\sharp_z:A\twoheadrightarrow B$ is a surjective local ring homomorphism.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 01QO (closed immersion criterion), with Schemes Tag 01HJ-area for the stalk map of a morphism of locally ringed spaces; the stalk identification is Sheaves, Lemma Tag 00AE as recorded in lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks

proof.text: By [def-weil-residue-field], the induced residue-field map is $A/\mathfrak m_A\to B/\mathfrak m_B$. It is surjective because $i^\sharp_z$ is surjective. Its kernel is zero: locality gives $(i^\sharp_z)^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B)=\mathfrak m_A$, so an element whose image lies in $\mathfrak m_B$ already lies in $\mathfrak m_A$. Therefore the homomorphism $\kappa(x)\to\kappa(z)$ is an isomorphism.
